title: Sprint-to-Production Activation Checklist and Threshold Catalog
content:
Purpose:
This is a working checklist and threshold catalog to take features from sprint branch to production activation. It focuses on measurable activation thresholds, quick go/no-go signals, lightweight mitigations and post-activation observability. Intended for product-ops + release engineers running weekly fast-path releases and for PMs preparing controlled activations.

Scope and assumptions:
- Covers small-to-medium feature activations (0.1% to 20% traffic ramp). Not intended for full platform migrations or infra-only upgrades.
- Assumes feature has passed QA and integration testing in staging, and security review sign-offs where applicable.
- Activation = enabling route + associated monitoring for a specified cohort.

Quick summary (one-line):
Activate when backend error rate < 0.5% (5xx), p50 latency within target, and quality regression score <= 1.5x baseline on core eval set. If any of the three fail during ramp, pause and trigger rollback checklist.

Activation thresholds (hard and soft):
- Traffic & capacity:
  - Soft: can sustain 2x expected peak qps for cohort during 10-min stress window.
  - Hard: 4x expected peak qps OR autoscaler fails to recover within 5 min -> abort activation.
- Latency:
  - Soft: p50 <= target_latency_ms * 1.2 over 15 min window.
  - Hard: p95 > target_latency_ms * 1.5 for two consecutive 5-min windows -> rollback.
- Errors:
  - Soft: 5xx rate < 1% and trending flat or down.
  - Hard: 5xx rate >= 2% OR error spike >= 0.5% absolute within 5 minutes -> pause and investigate.
- Quality/regression (model-specific):
  - Soft: automated eval delta (A/B prompts set) <= 2x allowed variance.
  - Hard: any P0 prompt failure pattern or regression > 3x allowed variance -> disable feature flag immediately.

Pre-activation checklist (owner initials required next to items):
- [ ] PM confirms acceptance criteria & canary prompts set (owner: PM)
- [ ] Product-ops configures cohort targeting (IP range / user segment / percentage)
- [ ] Release engineer verifies infra scaling plan and pre-warm run (owner: RE)
- [ ] SRE enables short-term increased log retention for 30m post-activation (owner: SRE)
- [ ] Observability: dashboards pinned, alert thresholds set, runbook link in Slack #ops (owner: observability)
- [ ] Security/compliance gate cleared if user data surface increases (owner: security)
- [ ] Feature flag exists and can be toggled via console/CLI (owner: Eng)
- [ ] Rollback steps documented and tested in staging (owner: Eng/QA)

Activation run sequence (recommended, time stamps relative to t0):
- t-60m: final sync with PM/RE/SRE in staging channel (quick checklist)
- t-15m: increase tracing sampling to 100% for cohort and enable debug logs for related services
- t0: enable flag for 0.5% traffic (cohort A)
- t+5m: check immediate signals (errors, latency p95, key KPI delta), if OK -> ramp
- t+15m: ramp to 2% (cohort B) and re-evaluate 
- t+30m: if stable, ramp to target exposure (e.g., 10%) and mark activation complete

Decision matrix (if anything hits a hard threshold):
- Hard threshold: toggle feature flag off, notify PM/RE/SRE, create incident ticket, attach traces and top 5 errors.
- Soft threshold: hold ramp for next 15m, assign owner to investigate, consider temporary traffic backoff 50% if unexplained trend persists.

Rollback and mitigation steps (quick):
1) Toggle flag off (CLI + console).
2) Confirm routing restored to baseline (smoketest endpoints).
3) Collect trace ids, sample logs, and save to incident ticket.
4) If rollback unsuccessful (symptoms persist), escalate to SRE on-call for network/infra investigation.

Post-activation validation (first 24h):
- Automated daily eval suite run against production samples (owner: applied-ml)
- Usage and cost delta report (token consumption per route) after 24h (owner: finance-ops)
- Customer support queue monitor for new issue patterns (owner: CS)
- Retrospective scheduled at +48 hours if any regression observed

KPIs to monitor (live dashboard suggestions):
- Activation success rate (activations that achieve target exposure without hitting hard thresholds)
- Time-to-detect (mean time between activation and first hard threshold breach)
- Mean time to rollback (flag off -> baseline confirmed)
- Quality delta (eval A/B score) and top P0 prompt regressions
- Cost per 1k tokens for the route versus baseline

Owner responsibilities matrix (short):
- PM: acceptance criteria, canary prompts, decision to continue/pause beyond 60m
- Release Engineer: flag toggles, infra pre-warm, rollback verification
- SRE: production monitoring, paging, and escalation
- Applied ML: eval set upkeep and automated regression detection
- Observability: dashboards + alert tuning

Notes and open questions (working):
- Should we add an automated short-circuit that reduces cohort by 75% (instead of full rollback) on first soft threshold hit? Pros/cons doc needed.
- Need runbook snippet for dedicated GPU-backed model variants where cold-starts can cause p95 spikes.
- Investigate a traffic-smoothing primitive in the routing layer to avoid instantaneous spikes during ramp.

Appendix: checklist templates and quick commands
- Toggle flag (CLI): rwctl feature toggle --on <flag> --cohort pct:0.5 --meta "sprint-123"
- Smoke test endpoints: /healthz, /predict?sample=smoke1, /predict?sample=canary2
- Minimal incident title template: [Activation][<feature>] Hard-Threshold hit - immediate rollback executed

Bottom line: This doc is intentionally lightweight and prescriptive. Use it for fast, repeatable activations and iterate after each run. Mark items as DONE in the doc and capture lessons in the activation retro thread.
